statement: From an effective size of 300, a seeded quasi-random search (scrambled Sobol) of 8 candidates, 16 from an effective size of 1,000, plus the standard settings, each scored by nested inner cross-validation, is enough to choose settings that predict at least as well as the standard settings, because the declared search spaces have low effective dimension, where random search is a strong baseline.
regime: prediction; searched families (boosted trees, XGBoost, forest); n_plan >= 300
decision: tuning plan: number of Sobol candidates S (8 / 16; halved under 'lighter')
user_sees: Nothing shown on screen beyond the family's methods text ('Its settings are searched inside every training fold'); the plan's counts are not surfaced yet.
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.2 'The strategy in v2' reason 3: random search is 'a surprisingly strong baseline' (Bischl et al. 2023; Bergstra & Bengio 2012); reasons 1-2 are replay and a known budget, not accuracy.
notes: [part id F1-002] searched_size at tuning.py:619; SobolStrategy at :728. SMALL_SAMPLE_STANDARD §5: at 1,000 rows a fixed conservative standard matched or beat the search's best of nine in 5 of 8 family-cells, so the budget may be too small to beat a good fixed setting (the standard candidate is included, so the search can never lose to the standard on the inner loss). [Merged P-sobol-random-search-adequate at docs/turbotab-next/RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md §4.2 ('The strategy in v2', reasons 3–4); its basis: Bischl et al. 2023 and Bergstra & Bengio 2012 (random search 'a surprisingly strong baseline'); Bischl et al. 2023 on halving.; its notes: Reasons 1–2 (replay, known budget) are engineering, not methods.]

statement: The signed paired difference between the interpretable benchmark (a properly specified regression with splines on the same in-fold preprocessing) and the best flexible family, with the flexible pick re-made in every bootstrap resample of the out-of-fold predictions (BBC-CV over the flexible set), estimates what interpretability costs or gains on the strictly proper primary and on calibration (distance of the calibration slope from 1) without the optimism of picking the best flexible family; when its 95% percentile interval spans 0 there is 'no measurable cost on these rows'.
regime: prediction; an interpretable benchmark and >=1 flexible family with out-of-fold predictions; >=10 scored rows
decision: the 'what the interpretable model costs or gains' readout (EXPLORE)
user_sees: "What the interpretable model costs or gains: … against the best of …, chosen anew in each of N resamples of the out-of-fold predictions (BBC-CV over the flexible set; positive favors …); … no measurable cost on these rows"
claimed_basis: Rudin 2019 (Nat Mach Intell 1:206): 'It is a myth that there is necessarily a trade-off between accuracy and interpretability'; the prediction review ('Remove the selection optimism of picking the "best flexible" family (BBC-CV over the flexible set)'); Tsamardinos et al. 2018 (selection.py:985-997).
notes: [part id F3-008] acceptance/test_explore_5_shelf.py::test_6_the_cost_or_gain_is_bbc_corrected_over_the_flexible_set replays the draws by hand (fidelity only). 'No measurable cost' when the interval spans 0 is an absence-of-evidence verdict. Calibration distance |1 - slope| is a convention. The benchmark itself is fixed (not chosen), so only the flexible side is corrected. [Merged F5-010 at turbotab/core/stages/evaluation.py:258-296; its basis: 'the review': 'Always fit the no-predictor baseline and a properly specified regression benchmark with splines' (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 rows 9 and 11).; its notes: turbotab/core/tests/acceptance/test_explore_5_shelf.py::test_5_the_regression_with_splines_benchmark_and_the_baseline_are_always_fitted_on_the_same_folds pins behavior. The benchmark has no interactions and no penalty; with many predictors and few events a spline on every continuous predictor can overfit, which the comparison would then misattribute.] [Merged F5-011 at turbotab/core/stages/evaluation.py:252-257; turbotab/core/models/validation.py:152 (P_OVER_N); its basis: none stated beyond least squares' non-uniqueness; P_OVER_N = 1.0 labeled a convention.; its notes: The check counts spec.inputs, not the spline-expanded columns: with k knots each continuous predictor adds k-2 columns, so the benchmark is non-unique well before p/n = 1 (e.g. p = n/3 with 5 knots), and it is still fitted there. test_explore_5_shelf.py::test_5_at_p_much_greater_than_n_no_benchmark... pins behavior.]

statement: For an energy-intake screen under Estimate, if the share of rows removed times the leavers' largest SMD on the adjustment set is below 0.003697, removing the screen (keeping every row) moves the exposure's estimate by less than 0.1 of its 95% interval half-width, so the app recommends 'Doesn't change your numbers here'; from 0.003697 it says 'could bias', and from 0.2 'act on it'.
regime: Dietary lens; Estimate or Describe; energy screen among the exclusions; rows_smd instrument marked calibrated

user_sees: "Doesn't change your numbers here" with reason "... That is below what would move the estimate; it is checked again after the plan is fixed."
claimed_basis: Calibration: 9 cases (Goldberg plus a ladder of 8 kcal range screens) from 'the dietary proof's simplified pipeline' on the NHANES fixture (complete cases, straight-line nutrients), one band-0 prediction that held (m_pre 0.0012 → m_post 0.011); band_1 lowered from the convention 0.05 to the smallest falsely reassured case; min_cases 5 (convention)
notes: [part id F6-007] Also materiality.py:1261-1310 (calibrate), 1034-1036 (band-0 text), materiality_cases.py. Threshold is fit in-sample to zero false reassurance on the same 9 cases from one table and one simplified pipeline; SURFACING_POLICY §2.6 requires the twelve reference journeys and a cry-wolf budget, neither used (the JSON 'about' admits the journeys are still to come). test_materiality.py::test_the_committed_calibration_reassures_falsely_on_none_of_its_cases is in-sample. Post-lock verify() relabels openly if the realized band is higher, which limits harm.

statement: Under complete-case analysis, rows are dropped only for blanks in the predictors the user has confirmed and kept. Blanks in a column whose blanks are coded as their own 'Missing' level are values, not missing data, and drop no row. A role that rode along unconfirmed drops no row, and the fit waits for its confirmation.
user_sees: Flow step "No predictor missing" with reason "a predictor has no value".
notes: Treating blanks as a category (the missing-indicator method) is known to bias adjusted estimates unless the missingness is structural (Greenland & Finkle 1995; Groenwold et al. 2012). The skip-pattern default in methods/missing.py (recommended_fills) relies on it, so a referee should pair the two claims. Other location: stages/rows.py:1445. | Inventory source id: F2-010.

statement: In a randomized trial, covariate adjustment only sharpens precision and causal wording is allowed; a case-control sample cannot give prevalence or absolute risk; matched sets are analyzed within each set; an observational study adjusts for confounders and speaks of associations.
decision: the design question, which gates adjustment and claim wording
user_sees: In a randomized trial adjustment only sharpens precision and causal wording is allowed; a case-control sample cannot give prevalence or absolute risk; matched sets are analyzed within each set.
claimed_basis: none stated (the drawer cites STROBE-nut only for naming the design)

statement: Under inference, a site that differs in both the exposure and the outcome confounds the estimate and intervals that treat its participants as independent are too narrow, so each site gets its own intercept and cluster-robust intervals (few groups needing a small-sample correction), 'cluster only' leaves between-group differences in the estimate, and under prediction validation keeps a group together.
